_README: AUTHORING TEMPLATE for one Case Study record.
Fill this in offline and hand it back; it maps 1:1 onto snapshot content paths.
Anything you omit simply hides that band on the page - a thin record still looks deliberate.
TWO THINGS THE SYSTEM WILL REFUSE, so do not spend time on them:
1. A metric with verification.class 'verified' and method 'self'. A self-report is
not third-party verification and the publish gate rejects it outright as a mislabel.
2. A verified metric with no evidenceId, or a headline metric with no baseline,
sample or methodology. A number with no account of how it was produced does not render.
The gate reads STRUCTURED fields. It does not read prose - so anything you write in a
narrative array is on your honour. That gap is a known open finding (V-29).

identity.title: Short, concrete, and about the outcome rather than the technology.
identity.standfirst: One sentence. The problem and what was built to solve it.

productionStatus._status_note: CORRECTED. This renders through the same label map as roadmap statuses, so it takes those values. Earlier drafts of this template said 'in_production | pilot | prototype' - none of those have a label and would render blank.

taxonomy.builtByType: colaberry_team | learner | intern | client_team | ai_flotation_team | joint_team
taxonomy._builtByType_note: CORRECTED. Earlier drafts offered 'client' and 'partner'; neither is a member of the union and both would be rejected. Note that ai_flotation_team is a real, separate value - which is what lets an AI Flotation surface tell a truthful story about a build it did not do, because attribution travels with the record rather than with the page.

situation._note: The problem, told so the READER recognises it as theirs. On Enterprise that is a buyer; on Training it is a prospective learner.
narrative: Paragraph 1 - the problem, stated as a business condition rather than a technology trend.
Paragraph 2 - why the obvious solutions fail.
Paragraph 3 - the harder version of the problem, the one worth solving.
constraints: A hard requirement the solution had to satisfy.
goals: What success would look like, in the client's terms.

architecture._note: What was BUILT. The software, not the methodology.
narrative: Paragraph 1 - the central mechanism, in one idea.
Paragraph 2 - the data or state that makes it work.
Paragraph 3 - a decision that was deliberate, and why.
stack: Auto-filled from the repository; override only to correct it.
architecture.diagramSource:
flowchart TD
  A["Input"] --> B["Process"]
  B --> C["Outcome"]
_diagramSource_rules: Mermaid source. Rendered client-side, themed to brand.
Angle brackets are REFUSED outright (the renderer writes to innerHTML).
Capped at 8000 characters. Keep node labels in double quotes.

measurement._note: What CHANGED. Narrative is for qualitative outcomes; metrics are for figures.
narrative: A qualitative outcome that is true and checkable, stated plainly.
Another. These carry the story where a number would be invented.

measurement.baseline: What it was before, and over what period.
measurement.sample: How much, how many, over what window.
measurement.methodology: How it was measured. Required for any headline figure.
limitations: What this figure does NOT prove. Stating one makes the rest credible.

heroMetrics: _note: MUST be the same object(s) as the isHeadline entries in measurement.metrics.
_note: A figure in the hero that is absent from measurement disappears from the page entirely.

roadmap.label: What shipped
roadmap._note: status carries done-ness; verification carries whether the STATEMENT is checkable. An item whose verification is 'pending' is DROPPED from the public page - the same rule that drops an unverified metric. Items admitting what is NOT solved are the most credible ones on the page.

artifacts.title: The learner command centre
artifacts.description: What the reader is looking at.

artifacts.title: Short, plain
artifacts.description: Atmosphere photography. Not a picture of this programme or its people.
artifacts._note: artifactType 'photo' is ATMOSPHERE and can never be evidence. It is ranked below screenshot and architecture for the hero, it renders labelled as atmosphere, and a photo whose title or description claims delivered work is DROPPED entirely. Two publicly-viewable images is the standard; the readiness rubric scores a record down below that.

_perSurface._note: Set per PUBLICATION, not on the record. This is how one record reads differently on two sites.
_perSurface.surfaceTitleOverride: A title written for THIS audience, or null to use the record's.
_perSurface.surfaceSummaryOverride: A standfirst written for THIS audience, or null.
